answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and let trust propagate through bounded-length random walks from independently anchored vertices. A Sybil cluster with few outgoing edges has low conductance, so only a small fraction of walk probability escapes it; with capped influence per vertex and an honest-anchor rule, its aggregate voting weight is bounded by that escape flow, not by its number of identities. A spiral of mutually endorsing accounts cannot turn a gale of internal edges into external trust.
